fact: TechAfrica News reports Orange Tunisia announced the operational launch of the MEDUSA submarine cable, landing at Bizerte, which Orange Tunisia owns along with the Tunisian section.

La Presse reports Orange Tunisie announced on 24 June 2026 that MEDUSA is in operational service via the Bizerte landing station, carrying its first international traffic; four fibre pairs of 24 Tbps each.
Connecting Africa reports Orange announced the ViaTunisia segment of MEDUSA, Marseille to Bizerte, is operational.
Orange states the ViaTunisia segment of MEDUSA, Marseille to Bizerte, reached Ready for Service on 3 June 2026.
Medusa describes its system as carrier-neutral, and Tunisie Telecom's CEO says the Bizerte landing raises Tunisie Telecom's international capacity eightfold, while Orange Tunisia hosts the landing.
Medusa's announcement of Tunisie Telecom's Medusa agreement says Tunisia's existing submarine cable links are PEACE, SeaMeWe-4, Didon and Hannibal (four cables; landing stations not named).
The Medusa press release states Orange Tunisia set up the Didon cable in 2014 linking Tunisia to Europe, in partnership with Ooredoo Tunisia.

INT decision 165/2013 orders the national operator to offer alternative operators regulated, cost-oriented access to international capacity (STM-1 to STM-64, priced) and co-location at its Bizerte landing station for Sea-Me-We 4 (Bizerte-Marseille).
The INT decision treats Sea-Me-We 4 (Bizerte-Marseille) as an operating cable whose international capacity is under-used.
TAP/Zawya says Tunisie Telecom already owns the Hannibal and SEA-ME-WE 4 submarine cables (landing stations not named).
Orange Tunisie says its Didon cable succeeded in 2014 (in service since 2014).

The US ITA commercial guide says Tunisie Telecom, the leading international connectivity provider, manages three sub-sea cables, including a Kelibia (Tunisia) to Mazara (Italy) cable; the other two are not named.
system: Kelibia-Mazara cable (three cables managed by Tunisie Telecom)
